title: SAML transient-claim refresh, admin-triggered reauth & session revocation spec
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem statement: Current SAML session handling at Redwood assumes immutable assertions for the life of a session. Real IdPs sometimes emit transient attributes (e.g., assurance_level, stepup_required, session_auth_time) or issue reauth/forceAuthn signals during a session. Additionally, admin actions (deprovision, change role binding, or explicit 'require reauth') must be enforceable immediately across the platform. This ticket defines behavior, logging, and controls for: (1) refreshing transient/ephemeral SAML claims mid-session, (2) admin-triggered reauthentication and forced logout, (3) graceful soft-logout/reauth windows for active flows, (4) RBAC v2 role-mapping re-evaluation, and (5) audit-event schema and retention required for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior: When an IdP signals stepup/forceAuthn or when Redwood receives an admin 'require_reauth' command, affected sessions must either (A) be marked 'reauth-required' and prompt the next request to redirect to IdP, or (B) be terminated immediately for high-risk admin actions. The policy that chooses A vs B must be configurable per customer and default to A with a 5-minute soft window.

JIT provisioning edge-case: If a user was JIT-provisioned and then deactivated at the IdP within the same session, the system must re-evaluate account state on first relevant request and prevent access if IdP now denies auth, logging both the original provision event and the deny event.

MFA expectations: If the IdP provides an assurance_level or mfa_claim indicating a step-up is required, the platform must surface a clear UX hook and record an audit event with the idp_event and required_level. Automated retries or silent refreshes are disallowed for step-up events without explicit user interaction.

RBAC v2 re-eval: Any role-binding changes in Redwood Console or via SCIM mapped attributes must trigger an on-next-request re-evaluation of roles. For admin-marked critical role changes, sessions holding the previous role must be marked for immediate reauth or terminated based on policy.

Audit logging: Audit events must be emitted for: idp_signal_received, session_marked_reauth_required, session_forced_logout, jitted_user_deactivated, role_binding_recalc, admin_initiated_reauth. Each event must include session_id, user_id, idp_event (if any), admin_actor (if any), old_roles, new_roles, correlation_id, and ISO8601 timestamp.

Testing: Automated integration tests covering IdP-initiated stepup, admin-forced reauth, JIT-provision->deactivate, and RBAC role-change flows. At least one fuzz test to ensure unknown transient claims do not crash session manager.

Documentation: Spec pages in Confluence updated with flow diagrams and console UX copy for reauth banners and admin controls. SDK docs updated to reflect new 401/409 responses indicating 'reauth_required' vs 'session_revoked'.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight session flag 'reauth_required' with an optional 'grace_window_seconds' to implement soft reauth. Default grace window=300s but configurable per-tenant.
Prefer marking sessions for reauth (soft approach) when IdP signals step-up or when role changes are non-critical; use immediate revocation for admin action types tagged 'high_risk' in the Console.
Do not attempt background silent SAML reauthentication: SAML flows require user interaction for MFA stepups, so platform must redirect and not silently refresh assertions.

Audit events will be appended to existing audit-log pipeline (structured JSON lines). To keep the schema flat for SIEM ingestion, fields will be string-valued; boolean fields encoded as 'true'/'false'.
RBAC v2: role-mapping updates will be applied to in-memory session role view on first request; we will not retroactively mutate cached token claims mid-request to avoid race conditions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy session flag and audit-event emitters to 5% of hosted-fleet. Monitor error rates and UX behavior for 72h.
Phase 2 (beta tenants): Opt-in customers can enable 'admin-force-reauth' via Console. Collect feedback from SEs and SOC teams.
Phase 3 (global): Enable default 'reauth_required' handling for all hosted tenants and release SDK changes. Coordinate Dedicated/Private release notes and a migration guide for self-hosted customers.
Rollout considerations: For Private deployments, provide a toggle and migration script to backfill 'session_metadata' table schema and add audit index.
monitoring_and_alerting: Track metric: sessions_marked_reauth_required_per_min by tenant. Alert if >500% baseline for a sustained 10m window (possible IdP outage or misconfiguration).
Track metric: sessions_forced_logout_rate and mean time from admin_action to session_revocation. Alert if >30s for >95th percentile in hosted mode.
Create dashboards: audit-events-by-type, reauth-latency-percentiles, failed-stepup-counts (broken MFA flows), and RBAC-recalc-failures.
Log sampling: sample 10% of full event payloads for 30 days for debugging while keeping storage reasonable; full structured events retained according to customer retention policy.
